nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be in $L^\infty(\mu)$, that is, $\mu$-almost everywhere strongly measurable and essentially bounded. Then $|\varphi(x)| \le \|\varphi\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}$ for $\mu$-almost every $x \in \alpha$.
nodes.title: Pointwise bound by the essential supremum norm

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be in $L^\infty(\mu)$, let $z \in \mathbb{C}$, and suppose the function $x \mapsto z - \varphi(x)$ is also in $L^\infty(\mu)$. For $\psi \in L^\infty(\mu)$ write $M_\psi$ for the multiplication operator $f \mapsto \psi f$ on $L^2(\mu)$. Then $z I - M_\varphi = M_{z - \varphi}$, where $I$ is the identity operator on…
nodes.title: Shifting a multiplication operator by a scalar

nodes.summary: Let $L^2([1,2])$ be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real functions for Lebesgue measure on $[1,2]$, with inner product $\langle f, g\rangle = \int_1^2 f(x)g(x)\,dx$. Let $T : L^2([1,2]) \to L^2([1,2])$ be a linear map such that for every $f$, $(Tf)(x) = x f(x)$ for almost every $x \in [1,2]$. Then $T$ is continuous and bijective, and $T = T^*$, where $T^*$ is the Hilbert space adjoint of $T$.
nodes.title: Multiplication by $x$ on $L^2((1,2))$ is bounded, bijective and self-adjoint

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi, \psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$. If $\varphi = \psi$ $\mu$-almost everywhere, then $\varphi$ and $\psi$ have the same essential range with respect to $\mu$.
nodes.title: The essential range is invariant under almost-everywhere equality

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ with $\mu(\alpha) \neq 0$, and let $c \in \mathbb{C}$. Then the essential range of the constant function $x \mapsto c$ with respect to $\mu$ is $\{c\}$.
nodes.title: Essential range of a constant function

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with a measurable structure in which singletons are measurable, and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$. Then the essential range of $\varphi$ with respect to counting measure on $\alpha$ is the range $\varphi(\alpha)$.
nodes.title: Essential range for counting measure on a finite type

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$. The essential range of $\varphi$ with respect to $\mu$ is the set of $z \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $\mu(\{x \in \alpha : |\varphi(x) - z| < \varepsilon\}) > 0$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.
nodes.title: Essential range

nodes.summary: Let $L^2([0,1])$ be the space of real square-integrable functions for Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$. There is a bounded linear operator $T : L^2([0,1]) \to L^2([0,1])$ such that for every $f \in L^2([0,1])$, $(Tf)(t) = t f(t)$ for almost every $t \in [0,1]$.
nodes.title: Multiplication by $t$ is bounded on $L^2((0,1))$

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be in $L^\infty(\mu)$, that is, $\mu$-almost everywhere strongly measurable and essentially bounded. Then there is a measurable $\psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ such that $\varphi = \psi$ $\mu$-almost everywhere and $\psi$ is in $L^\infty(\mu)$.
nodes.title: Measurable representatives of essentially bounded functions

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $t \subseteq \alpha$ be a measurable set with $0 < \mu(t) < \infty$. Then there is $u \in L^2(\mu)$ (complex valued) with $\|u\| = 1$ such that $u(x) = \mu(t)^{-1/2}$ for $\mu$-almost every $x \in t$ and $u(x) = 0$ for $\mu$-almost every $x \notin t$.
nodes.title: Normalized indicator of a set of finite positive measure

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be measurable and in $L^\infty(\mu)$, and let $M_\varphi$ be the multiplication operator $f \mapsto \varphi f$ on $L^2(\mu)$. Then $z \in \mathbb{C}$ is an eigenvalue of $M_\varphi$ if and only if $\mu(\{x \in \alpha : \varphi(x) = z\}) > 0$.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a multiplication operator on $L^2$, measurable multiplier

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be in $L^\infty(\mu)$, and let $M_\varphi$ be the multiplication operator $f \mapsto \varphi f$ on $L^2(\mu)$. Then $z \in \mathbb{C}$ is an eigenvalue of $M_\varphi$ if and only if $\mu(\{x \in \alpha : \varphi(x) = z\}) > 0$.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a multiplication operator on $L^2$

nodes.summary: $L^2([1,2])$ is the space of real-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$ that are square-integrable for Lebesgue measure restricted to $[1,2]$, taken modulo equality almost everywhere on $[1,2]$.
nodes.title: The space $L^2((1,2))$

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $\varphi \colon \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be an essentially bounded, almost everywhere strongly measurable function, and let $M_\varphi$ be the multiplication operator $f \mapsto \varphi f$ on $L^2(\mu)$. If $C \ge 0$ is a real number and $f \in L^2(\mu)$ satisfies $\|f\| = 1$ and $C\,|f(x)| \le |\varphi(x)|\,|f(x)|$ for $\mu$-almost every $x$, then…
nodes.title: Lower bound for the norm of a multiplication operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi, \psi \colon \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be essentially bounded, almost everywhere strongly measurable functions. If $\varphi = \psi$ $\mu$-almost everywhere, then the multiplication operators $M_\varphi$ and $M_\psi$ on $L^2(\mu)$ are equal.
nodes.title: Multiplication operators with almost everywhere equal multipliers coincide

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $c \in \mathbb{C}$. The multiplication operator on $L^2(\mu)$ by the constant function $x \mapsto c$ sends every $f \in L^2(\mu)$ to the scalar multiple $c f$.
nodes.title: Multiplication by a constant function on $L^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and, for an essentially bounded, almost everywhere strongly measurable function $\chi \colon \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$, let $M_\chi$ be the multiplication operator $f \mapsto \chi f$ on $L^2(\mu)$. Let $\varphi, \psi \colon \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be essentially bounded, almost everywhere strongly measurable functions such that the pointwise product…
nodes.title: Product of multiplication operators

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$. The multiplication operator on $L^2(\mu)$ by the constant function $1$ is the identity operator.
nodes.title: Multiplication by one is the identity

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi \colon \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be an essentially bounded, almost everywhere strongly measurable function. The multiplication operator $M_\varphi$ is the continuous $\mathbb{C}$-linear operator on $L^2(\mu)$ that sends $f$ to the class of the pointwise product $x \mapsto \varphi(x) f(x)$.
nodes.title: Multiplication operator on $L^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $c \in \mathbb{C}$. The constant function $x \mapsto c$ belongs to $\mathcal{L}^\infty(\mu)$: it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and essentially bounded.
nodes.title: Constant functions are essentially bounded

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $\varphi \colon \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be an essentially bounded, almost everywhere strongly measurable function, and let $f \in L^2(\mu)$. Then the pointwise product $x \mapsto \varphi(x) f(x)$, formed with a representative of $f$, belongs to $\mathcal{L}^2(\mu)$: it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and square integrable.
nodes.title: An essentially bounded multiple of an $L^2$ function is in $L^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $\varphi \colon \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be an essentially bounded, almost everywhere strongly measurable function, and let $M_\varphi$ be the multiplication operator on $L^2(\mu)$. If $C$ is a real number with $|\varphi(x)| \le C$ for $\mu$-almost every $x$, then $\|M_\varphi f\| \le C \|f\|$ for every $f \in L^2(\mu)$.
nodes.title: Almost everywhere bound for a multiplication operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $\varphi \colon \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be an essentially bounded, almost everywhere strongly measurable function, and let $M_\varphi$ be the multiplication operator on $L^2(\mu)$. If $C$ is a real number and $f \in L^2(\mu)$ is such that, for $\mu$-almost every $x$, either $|\varphi(x)| \le C$ or $f(x) = 0$, then $\|M_\varphi f\| \le C \|f\|$.
nodes.title: Bound for a multiplication operator on the support of a vector

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be in $L^\infty(\mu)$, with essential supremum norm $\|\varphi\|_\infty$. Then the multiplication operator $M_\varphi$ on the complex space $L^2(\mu)$ has operator norm $\|M_\varphi\| \le \|\varphi\|_\infty$.
nodes.title: Norm bound for multiplication operators on L²

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be a measurable function in $L^\infty(\mu)$, with essential supremum norm $\|\varphi\|_\infty$. Then the multiplication operator $M_\varphi$ on the complex space $L^2(\mu)$ has operator norm $\|M_\varphi\| = \|\varphi\|_\infty$.
nodes.title: Norm of an L² multiplication operator with measurable multiplier

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be in $L^\infty(\mu)$, with essential supremum norm $\|\varphi\|_\infty$. Then the multiplication operator $M_\varphi$ on the complex space $L^2(\mu)$ has operator norm $\|M_\varphi\| = \|\varphi\|_\infty$.
nodes.title: Norm of a multiplication operator on L²

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ and let $z \in \mathbb{C}$. Then $z$ is not in the essential range of $\varphi$ with respect to $\mu$ if and only if there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the preimage under $\varphi$ of the open ball $B(z, \varepsilon) = \{w \in \mathbb{C} : |w - z| < \varepsilon\}$ has $\mu$-measure zero.
nodes.title: Points outside the essential range

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be a measurable function in $L^\infty(\mu)$. Then the spectrum of the multiplication operator $M_\varphi$, as an element of the complex algebra of bounded operators on $L^2(\mu)$, equals the essential range of $\varphi$ with respect to $\mu$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of an L² multiplication operator with measurable multiplier

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ be in $L^\infty(\mu)$. Then the spectrum of the multiplication operator $M_\varphi$, as an element of the complex algebra of bounded operators on $L^2(\mu)$, equals the essential range of $\varphi$ with respect to $\mu$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of a multiplication operator on L²

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
